accepted.question_text: For a closed manifold M of dimension at least 2, does there exist a collection of complete invariants that classifies real-analytic diffeomorphisms f:M→M up to topological conjugacy, and is the topological conjugacy relation on the space Diff^ω(M) of real-analytic diffeomorphisms a Borel equivalence relation?

evidence.quote: Question 1.1 (Gorodetski). Is there a way to provide a classification of real analytic diffeomorphisms Diffω (M ) of a given closed manifold M , dim M ≥ 2, by complete invariants? Is the equivalence relation on Diffω (M ) given by topological conjugacy Borel?

accepted.question_text: Let M be a closed manifold. Can the space of Kupka-Smale diffeomorphisms of M, meaning diffeomorphisms whose periodic orbits are all hyperbolic and whose stable and unstable manifolds meet transversally, be classified up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants, and is topological conjugacy on that Kupka-Smale subspace a Borel equivalence relation?

evidence.quote: Question 1.2 (Gorodetski). Can the space of Kupka-Smale diffeomorphisms of a given closed manifold be classified up to topological conjugacy by complete invariants? Is topological conjugacy a Borel equivalence relation in the space of Kupka-Smale diffeomorphisms?

accepted.question_text: For a closed manifold M with dim M ≥ 2, does there exist an open dense subset, or at least a dense Gδ subset, of Diff^∞(M) on which the equivalence relation of topological conjugacy is Borel?

evidence.quote: Question 1.3 (Gorodetski). Is there an open dense subset (or a dense Gδ subset) in Diff∞ (M ), dim M ≥ 2, such that the equivalence relation given by topological conjugacy on the subset is Borel?

accepted.question_text: What is the descriptive-set-theoretic complexity of the topological conjugacy relation on Axiom A dynamical systems?

evidence.quote: Question 1.4 (Foreman). What is the complexity of the relation of topological conjugacy of Axiom A systems?

accepted.question_text: Let C be the class of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold that are topologically conjugate to a structurally stable diffeomorphism, and let E be topological conjugacy restricted to C. Is E Borel reducible to equality?

evidence.quote: Question 1.5 (Foreman). Let C be the collection of diffeomorphisms of a compact manifold M that are topologically conjugate to a structurally stable diffeomorphism. Let E be the relation of topological conjugacy restricted to C. Is E Borel reducible to ≈ (equality relation)?

accepted.question_text: Is the topological conjugacy relation on the class of all Cantor minimal systems a Borel equivalence relation?

evidence.quote: Question 1.6 (Gao). Is the topological conjugacy relation for all Cantor minimal systems Borel?

accepted.question_text: Is the topological flip-conjugacy relation on the class of all Cantor minimal systems a Borel equivalence relation?

evidence.quote: Question 1.7 (Gao). Is the topological flip conjugacy relation for all Cantor minimal systems Borel?

accepted.question_text: For minimal subshifts, is the topological conjugacy relation hyperfinite, or is it a universal countable Borel equivalence relation?

evidence.quote: Question 1.8 (Gao). Is the topological conjugacy relation for all minimal subshifts hyperfinite or a universal countable Borel equivalence relation?

accepted.question_text: Is there an algorithm that decides whether two subshifts of finite type are topologically conjugate by homeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 1.9 (Foreman). Is there an algorithm for determining whether two subshifts of finite type are conjugate by homeomorphisms?

accepted.question_text: For smooth dynamical systems in dimension 2, if one discards only Lebesgue-null sets and uses metric entropy instead of topological entropy, does one still obtain a Borel classification statement analogous to the almost-Borel classification discussed for surface diffeomorphisms?

evidence.quote: Question 1.15 (Buzzi). I conjecture that a similar statement also holds when discarding only sets of zero Lebesgue measure using metric entropy instead of topological entropy (see [36]), at least in dimension 2 where we have the recent result [6].

accepted.question_text: Is the measure-isomorphism relation, when restricted to K-automorphisms, a Borel equivalence relation, and is it Borel reducible to an action of S∞?

evidence.quote: Question 1.16 (Newberger). Is measure isomorphism restricted to K-automorphisms a Borel equivalence relation? Can it be reduced to an S∞ -action?

accepted.question_text: Is the measure-isomorphism relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations of the unit interval Borel bi-reducible with the maximal Polish group action?

evidence.quote: Question 1.17. Is the measure isomorphism relation on ergodic measure-preserving transformations of the unit interval bi-reducible with the maximal Polish group action?

accepted.question_text: Where does Kakutani equivalence on ergodic measure-preserving transformations lie in the hierarchy of analytic equivalence relations, and is this relation Borel reducible to an action of S∞?

evidence.quote: Question 1.18. Where does the Kakutani equivalence relation on ergodic measurepreserving transformations sit among the analytic equivalence relations? Is it reducible to an S∞ -action?

accepted.question_text: For integers k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1, what is the descriptive complexity of the class CPE^k(T^n) of C^k self-maps of the n-torus with completely positive entropy, meaning that every nontrivial factor has positive topological entropy?

evidence.quote: Question 2.2 (García-Ramos). Let k ≥ 1 and n ≥ 1. What is the complexity of CPEk (Πn )?

evidence.quote: Question 2.5 (García-Ramos). Let k ≥ 0 and n ≥ 2. Is CPEk (Πn ) ∩ Mix Borel?

accepted.question_text: For a fixed Kakutani equivalence class of measure-preserving systems, is that class a Borel set, and if it is, what is the complexity of the isomorphism relation restricted to that class?

accepted.question_text: Let X be the space of continuous actions of the free group F2 on two generators. Is the subset consisting of actions that are measure-isomorphic to Bernoulli F2-actions a Borel set, and is the analogous collection of Borel actions also Borel?

evidence.quote: Question 3.1 (Foreman). Let X be the space of continuous actions of the free group F2 on two generators. Is the collection of Bernoulli actions measure isomorphic to Bernoulli F2 -actions a Borel set? (Borel actions?)

accepted.question_text: Let X_2 be the free part of the full shift {0,1}^{Z^2} with its shift action σ, let X_H be the space of directed bi-infinite Hamiltonian paths in Z^2, and let Φ:X_2→X_H be a Borel Z^2-equivariant map whose existence yields an orbit-equivalent Z-action T_Φ on X_2. Can Φ be chosen so that for every pair μ,ν of σ-invariant ergodic probability measures on X_2, the measure-preserving Z^2-systems (X_2,μ,σ) and (X_2,ν,σ) are conjugate if and only if the induced Z-systems (X_2,μ,T_Φ) and (X_2,ν,T_Φ) are conjugate?
accepted.context_brief: Conjugacy for Z^2 via Hamiltonian paths

evidence.quote: Question 3.3 (Chandgotia). Can Φ be chosen such that for all µ, ν ∈ Me , (X2 , µ, σ) is conjugate to (X2 , ν, σ) if and only if (X2 , µ, TΦ ) is conjugate to (X2 , ν, TΦ )?

accepted.question_text: Is the conjugation action of the Polish group Aut(X,μ) of measure-preserving automorphisms of a standard probability space on itself a complete orbit equivalence relation, meaning that every orbit equivalence relation is Borel reducible to it?

evidence.quote: Conjecture 4.1 (Sabok). The action of Aut(X, µ) on itself by conjugation is a complete orbit equivalence relation.

accepted.question_text: Let T0 be an ergodic measure-preserving transformation and [T0] its full group. If T1 and T2 are Bernoulli shifts with equal entropy and with the same orbit partition as T0, does there exist T∈[T0] such that T1 = T T2 T^{-1}?
accepted.context_brief: Bernoulli conjugacy inside a full group

evidence.quote: Question 4.2 (Thouvenot). Let T1 , T2 be two Bernoulli shifts with equal entropy, suppose that they have the same orbits as T0 . Is there T ∈ [T0 ] such that T1 = T T2 T −1 ?

accepted.question_text: Does the conjugacy relation on Aut(X,μ) Borel reduce to the conjugacy relation on the full group [T0] of an ergodic transformation T0, and does such a reduction still exist after restricting both sides to ergodic transformations?

evidence.quote: Question 4.3. Does the conjugacy relation on Aut(X, µ) Borel reduce to the conjugacy relation on [T0 ]? Does it when we restrict to ergodic transformations?

accepted.question_text: Is the conjugation action of Aut(X,μ) on itself unbalanced in the sense of dynamical turbulence, and does this remain true after restricting to ergodic transformations?

evidence.quote: Question 4.4. Is the conjugacy action of Aut(X, µ) on itself unbalanced? If yes, is it still if we restrict to ergodic transformations?

accepted.question_text: Is the conjugacy relation on the full group [T0] Borel, and if not, does it become Borel when restricted to ergodic transformations?

evidence.quote: Question 4.5. Is the conjugacy relation on [T0 ] Borel? If no, is it when restricted to ergodic transformations?

accepted.question_text: For topological full groups arising from continuous actions of Polish groups on compact Polish spaces, especially from actions of the real line, what structural and classification properties hold? In particular, when are these groups coarsely bounded, when do they admit a dense finitely generated subgroup, how many non-isomorphic such groups are there, and can one classify the underlying actions by homeomorphisms?
accepted.context_brief: Topological full groups of Polish actions

evidence.quote: Question 4.6. What can we say about these topological full groups, especially when the acting group is the real line? For instance, when are they coarsely bounded in the sense of [37]? When do they admit a dense finitely generated group2 ? How many such groups are there3 ? Can one classify their actions by homeomorphisms?

accepted.question_text: Let Auth_{<∞}(I,λ) be the space of finite-entropy measure-preserving automorphisms of the Lebesgue interval and Diff(T^n,λ^n) the space of Lebesgue-preserving diffeomorphisms of the n-torus. Does there exist a Borel map G from Auth_{<∞}(I,λ) into the union over n of Diff(T^n,λ^n) such that each system (I,λ,T) is measure-isomorphic to (T^n,λ^n,G(T))?

evidence.quote: Question 5.1 (Rodriguez Hertz). Is there a Borel map G : Auth<∞ (I, λ) → Diff(Πn , λn ), such that (I, λ, T ) is isomorphic to (Πn , λn , G(T )).

accepted.question_text: Can every non-periodic odometer be realized smoothly, for example by a smooth dynamical system on a compact manifold?

evidence.quote: It is still open if any (non-periodic) odometer can be smoothly realized.

accepted.question_text: With the same notation as above, does there exist a Borel map G from finite-entropy measure-preserving automorphisms of the Lebesgue interval into Lebesgue-preserving toral diffeomorphisms such that each source system is Kakutani equivalent to its image system?

evidence.quote: Question 5.2 (Rodriguez Hertz). Is there a Borel map G : Auth<∞ (I, λ) → Diff(Πn , λn ), such that (I, λ, T ) is Kakutani equivalent to (Πn , λn , G(T )).

evidence.quote: Question 5.3 (Rodriguez Hertz). If a measure-preserving system is Kakutani realizable can we conclude it is also isomorphically realizable?

accepted.question_text: Does every measure-preserving action of a free group admit a uniquely ergodic topological model?

evidence.quote: Question 5.4 (Seward). Do we have uniquely ergodic topological models for every measure-preserving group action of a free group?
